tools.name: check_business
tools.description: Use this when the user names a specific US business and asks whether it is legitimate, licensed, or safe to pay, what public records exist on it, or what to check before signing a quote, paying a deposit, sending money, or paying a business that is asking them for money, such as a debt collector. Co

tools.name: compare_businesses
tools.description: Use this when the user explicitly asks to compare public records for two to five specific businesses of the same offered kind in one city/state before signing or paying. Returns a table of the kind's record types with each business's dated sources, unavailable labels, limits and identity candidates.

tools.name: check_mover
tools.description: Compatibility alias for check_business with kind=movers. Returns the same dated mover records; no verdict, rating or recommendation.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_business · Private data: check_business, compare_businesses, check_mover · Public sink: check_business.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_business · Private data: check_business, compare_businesses, check_mover · Public sink: check_business

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
